title: [Audit] Failed sign-ins and denied access
description: The newest 1,000 failed sign-ins and requests refused or failed after sign-in, newest first. Discover stops at 1,000 rows, so on a busy range the result count is that cap; the Failed or denied tile counts them all. Result says which kind each row is: a failed sign-in (authentication_failed, realm_authentication_failed, anonymous_access_denied: someone who could not prove who they are), denied (access_denied: an authenticated identity hitting a permission wall), or failed (any other action whose outcome is failure). Credential is how the request authenticated; Kibana events record none. An Identity that reads as an opaque id is a principal whose events carry no email and no key name — usually an organisation-level Elastic Cloud API key, which the audit stream records only by its id.
esql: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") OR attributes.event.outcome == "failure" | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 1000 | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | EVAL auth = CASE(attributes.authentication.type == "api_key", "API key", attributes.authentication.type == "token", "Token", attributes.authentication.type == "realm", "Realm", attributes.authentication.type == "saml", "SAML", attributes.authentication.type == "anonymous", "Anonymous", attributes.authentication.type == "internal", "Internal", attributes.authentication.type), result = CASE(attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied"), "failed sign-in", attributes.event.action == "access_denied", "denied", "failed") | KEEP @timestamp, actor, attributes.event.action, result, auth, client.geo.country_iso_code, client.ip | RENAME @timestamp AS Time, actor AS Identity, attributes.event.action AS Action, result AS Result, auth AS Credential, client.geo.country_iso_code AS Country, client.ip AS `Client IP`
